fields.Notes:
Deepseek : can you explain why 二十歳 is read はたち?
Certainly! The reading of 二十歳 as はたち is a fascinating example of how Japanese numbers and age-related terms can have unique or historical pronunciations. Let’s break it down:

Why is 二十歳 read as はたち?

  1. Historical Pronunciation:
    • In Old Japanese, the number 20 was pronounced as はた (hata). This is an archaic reading that has largely fallen out of use in modern Japanese, except in specific contexts like age.
    • The suffix ち (chi) was added to indicate "age" or "years old." This is similar to how さい (sai) is used in modern Japanese for ages (e.g., 二十歳 = にじゅっさい).
    So, はた (20) + ち (age) became はたち to mean "20 years old."
  2. Special Case for Age 20:
    • In Japanese culture, turning 20 (はたち) is a significant milestone because it marks the age of adulthood. This is celebrated in the 成人式 (seijin-shiki), or "Coming of Age Ceremony."
    • Because of its cultural importance, the unique reading はたち has been preserved specifically for this age.
  3. Modern Usage:
    • While はたち is the traditional and most common reading for 二十歳, it can also be read as にじゅっさい in modern Japanese. However, はたち carries a more formal or traditional nuance and is often preferred in ceremonial or literary contexts.

Comparison with Other Age Readings:

  • Most ages in Japanese use the standard counter さい (sai):
    • 10 years old = じゅっさい
    • 30 years old = さんじゅっさい
  • However, 20 years old is unique because it retains the older reading はたち alongside the modern にじゅっさい.

fields.Notes:
Grammar Point: てみたい

Structure: Verbて-form + みる + たい
  • てみる: "Try doing (something)"
  • たい: "Want to do (something)"
Combined Meaning:
"Want to try doing (something)"
→ Expresses a desire to experience something new or hypothetical.

Translation of the Full Sentence

Japanese:
今よりもっと大きくなって
一人でどこへでも行けるようになったら
遠い国に行ってみたい｡
遠い島に行ってみたい｡
English:
"When I grow bigger than I am now
and become able to go anywhere alone,
I’d like to try visiting a distant country.
I’d like to try visiting a distant island."

Nuance Breakdown

  1. 行ってみたい ≠ Just "want to go" (行きたい).
    • It implies:
      • Curiosity ("I wonder what it’s like...").
      • First-time experience ("I’ve never been, but I want to try").

Key Examples

  • 食べてみたい = "I want to try eating (it)."
  • やってみたい = "I want to try doing (it)."
This grammar is common in dreams, wishes, or bucket lists!
Care, there are two similar looking "meet" kanji : 
会:meeting, meet, party, association, interview, join
合:fit, suit, join, 0.1
both can have the reading あ.う
会[あ]う : 5-dan; intransitive, to meet; to encounter
合[あ]う : 5-dan; intransitive, to come together; to merge; to unite; to meet

    １７画　馬部　［人名漢字］
    区点＝２９５７　１６進＝３Ｄ５９　シフトＪＩＳ＝８Ｆ７８

    《音読み》　シュン

    《訓読み》　すみやか（すみやかなり）

    《名付け》　たかし・とし・はやお・はやし

    《意味》
    （１）｛名｝すらりと背が高く、足のはやい馬。「駿馬シュンメ」
    （２）シュンタリ｛形｝すぐれてりっぱである。俊。「駿才シュンサイ（＝俊才）」「駿雄シュンユウ（＝俊雄）」
    （３）シュンタリ｛形｝高くそびえている。偉大である。「駿命シュンメイ」
    （４）シュンタリ｛形｝すみやか（スミヤカナリ）。すばやい。「駿奔走在廟＝駿トシテ奔走シテ廟ニ在リ」〔詩経〕

    《解字》
    会意兼形声。右側の字（音シュン）は「允＋夂」の会意文字で、すらりとした人をあらわす。駿はそれを音符とし、馬をそえた字で、すらりと背の高い、という意味を含む。

    《単語家族》
    俊と同系。

    《熟語》
